title: Through Our Own Filters
introduction:
我觉得人们看到的东西其实都不是完全客观的，我们会根据自己的经历、记忆和当下的感受去理解眼前的东西，同时也会在这个过程中主动或者不自觉地过滤掉一些自己不想接收、不想面对，或者觉得不重要的信息。
有时候我们并不是没有看到，而是选择忽略了。我们看到的可能只是自己愿意看到的那一部分，然后再用自己的经验或者想象去补全剩下的部分。所以同一件事情，不同的人可能会有完全不同的理解。
我也觉得这种过滤不只是发生在看东西的时候，它也存在于我们对人的认识、对记忆的理解，甚至存在于对自己的自我认识里。我们会保留一些片段，也会忘记或者刻意避开另一些不想面对或接受的片段。最后留在脑海里的，并不一定是真实发生过的全部，而是经过自己一次次选择和理解之后留下来的版本。
introduction-en:
Our understanding of the world is shaped by personal experience, memory, and emotion. Faced with the same thing, we retain different details, overlook others, and fill in the gaps with assumptions or imagination. This project explores how such filtering operates within perception and extends to our understanding of others, the past, and ourselves.
I investigate this process through two installations. In the first, moving images of liquids are projected onto layers of gauze, transforming as light passes through and images overlap. In the second, translucent surfaces obscure familiar objects, including bamboo and a candelabrum, making them difficult to identify. A screen embedded in sand displays imagery of liquids and skies, while mirrors repeat both the sand and the moving images, creating an unsettling interplay between objects, images, and reflections.
Viewers must interpret what they see through partial visual clues, while obstruction and reflection continually complicate their judgements. The work asks how much of the world we perceive comes from what is before us, and how much we construct through our own choices and expectations.
